title: Burning oil smell
h1: Why does my car smell like burning oil?
metaDesc: Car smells like burning oil? Answer a few questions to see if it's a leak onto the exhaust, spilled oil or oil burning inside the engine, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: burning oil smell after oil change
smell of burning oil from engine
car smells like oil when ac is on
car smells like oil when heater is on
car smell burning oil when stopped
intro: A burning oil smell usually means oil is landing on something hot, most often the exhaust. Sometimes it's just spilled oil after an oil change, and sometimes the engine is burning oil inside. A few questions will tell you which, and how quickly you need to act.
safety: If you see smoke from under the hood, pull over, turn off the engine and step away from the car. Call 911 if you see flames.
If the oil pressure light comes on, pull over and turn off the engine right away.
If the engine starts knocking or ticking loudly, pull over and turn it off.

q_danger.q: Is there smoke from under the hood, or is the oil pressure light on?
q_danger.help: The oil pressure light usually looks like a red oil can with a drip. A faint whiff of smoke after parking is different from smoke you can see while driving.

opts.a: Yes, visible smoke from under the hood
The oil pressure or low oil light is on
No, but there's blue-gray smoke from the tailpipe
No smoke and no warning lights

q_recent.q: Has the car had an oil change or engine work in the last few days?

q_level.q: With the engine off and the car on level ground, what does the oil dipstick show?
q_level.help: Pull the dipstick (usually a yellow or orange handle), wipe it, push it all the way back in, then pull it out and read where the oil reaches between the two marks. Some newer cars show oil level on the dashboard instead.

opts.a: The level is fine and I don't see drips under the car
The level is low and there are oily spots under the car
The level is low, but I don't see any drips
It's below the lowest mark, or there's no oil on the stick at all
I'm not sure, or I can't check it

result.title: Oil may be burning on hot engine parts. Treat it as a fire risk
result.now: Pull over, turn off the engine and step away from the car. Don't open the hood if you see flames. Have it towed.
if: If you see flames, get everyone away from the car and call 911.
If the smoke stops once the engine cools and you find a cap or dipstick that wasn't secured, the oil level and any spilled oil still need checking before you drive.
If the oil pressure light came on or the temperature gauge is high, don't restart the engine.
result.why: Visible smoke usually means a fair amount of oil is hitting very hot parts. Engine oil can ignite on a hot exhaust, and a leak big enough to smoke can also run the engine low on oil.

causes.name: Major valve cover or gasket leak
causes.clues: Oil running down the side of the engine onto the exhaust.

causes.name: Oil filler cap left off or loose
causes.clues: Oil sprayed around the top of the engine, often after an oil change.

causes.name: Oil filter or line leak
causes.clues: Oil sprayed under the engine, and the oil level dropping fast.

causes.name: A different fluid, like power steering or transmission fluid
causes.clues: The oil level is fine, but another fluid is low.

shop: Exhaust and heat shield inspection for oil residue

result.title: The engine may be running low on oil or losing oil pressure
result.now: Pull over and turn off the engine. Don't restart it until you've checked the oil level. If it's empty or the light stays on, have it towed.
if: If the oil level was very low and topping it up makes the light go off, don't assume the engine is undamaged. Have it checked before relying on the car, and ask the shop whether it should be towed in.
If the engine was knocking or ticking loudly, don't restart it.
If you see smoke from under the hood, step away from the car.
result.why: A burning oil smell plus an oil pressure light often means a leak has drained enough oil that the engine isn't being protected. Running an engine without oil pressure can destroy it within minutes.

causes.name: Major oil leak
causes.clues: Oil on the ground, on the engine, or smoke.

causes.name: Engine burning a lot of oil
causes.clues: Blue-gray exhaust smoke and no visible leak.

causes.name: Failed oil pump or pressure sensor
causes.clues: The oil level is full but the light is still on. A shop will usually test oil pressure with a gauge before replacing the sensor or pump.

you: Wait a few minutes after shutting off, then check the dipstick.

result.title: The engine may be burning oil internally
result.now: Check the oil level, top it up to the full mark if needed, and get it checked within a few days. Check the level every time you fill up until then.
if: If the oil drops below the lowest mark between checks, don't drive it until it's topped up.
If the check engine light flashes or the engine runs rough, get it checked right away. Oil can foul the spark plugs and damage the catalytic converter.
If the oil pressure light comes on or the engine starts knocking, pull over and shut it off right away.
result.why: When oil gets past worn seals or rings, it burns with the fuel and leaves as blue-gray exhaust smoke with a burning oil smell. The level often drops with no drips under the car. A shop will usually check the crankcase ventilation (PCV) system first, since it's a simpler fix than internal engine work.

causes.name: Stuck or clogged PCV valve
causes.clues: Oil use started suddenly, or there's oil in the air intake.

causes.name: Worn valve stem seals
causes.clues: A puff of blue smoke on startup or after idling, then it clears.

causes.name: Worn piston rings
causes.clues: Steady blue smoke when accelerating, often on a high-mileage engine.

causes.name: Leaking turbocharger seals (turbo engines)
causes.clues: Blue smoke and oil in the intake piping.

you: Track how much oil you add and over how many miles.
Notice whether the smoke shows at startup or while accelerating.
shop: Spark plug inspection for oil fouling

result.title: Oil spilled during the service may be burning off
result.now: Check the oil level, make sure the filler cap is tight and the dipstick is fully seated, and look under the car for fresh drips. If everything looks right, watch whether the smell fades over the next few drives.
if: If you see fresh drips, or the smell gets stronger instead of fading, have the shop recheck the oil filter and drain plug right away.
If you see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil level is low or the oil pressure light comes on, don't drive it. Call the shop that did the work.
result.why: It's easy to spill a little oil on the engine or exhaust during an oil change. It can smell for a few drives, then fade. A loose filter, drain plug or cap is the thing to rule out, and the shop that did the work can recheck it quickly.

causes.name: Spilled oil burning off
causes.clues: The smell is fading day by day, and there are no drips.

causes.name: Loose or double-gasketed oil filter
causes.clues: Fresh oil drips under the front of the engine.

causes.name: Loose drain plug or filler cap
causes.clues: Oil on the bottom of the engine, or sprayed around the cap.

you: Check the oil level and filler cap.
Put cardboard under the engine overnight.
shop: Recheck the oil filter and drain plug
Clean spilled oil off the engine and exhaust

result.title: A slow oil seep onto the exhaust, often from the valve cover gasket
result.now: Look for oily residue on top and down the sides of the engine, check the oil level weekly, and book a check.
if: If the oil level starts dropping or you see drips, get it checked within a few days.
If you see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the oil pressure light comes on or the engine starts knocking, pull over and shut it off right away.
result.why: A very small leak can drip onto the exhaust and cook, giving a strong smell long before the oil level drops. The valve cover gasket on top of the engine is a common source. A shop will usually clean the area or use dye to confirm the source before replacing a gasket.

causes.name: Valve cover gasket seep
causes.clues: Oily residue along the top edge of the engine.

causes.name: Oil filter housing or cooler gasket
causes.clues: Residue near the oil filter.

causes.name: Oil from a past spill or overfill
causes.clues: An oil change in the last few weeks.

you: Look for wet, oily areas on the engine with a flashlight.
shop: Dye test if the source isn't clear

result.title: An active oil leak may be reaching hot parts
result.now: Don't keep using the car until the leak is checked. Top up the oil to the full mark with the type in your owner's manual, then have it towed or ask a mobile mechanic to look at it.
if: If the oil level drops noticeably after the engine runs for a short time, don't run it again.
If you see smoke from under the hood or the oil light comes on, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
If the engine knocks or ticks loudly, don't start it again until it's checked.
result.why: A low oil level plus spots under the car means oil is escaping fast enough to matter. It can run the engine low and, if it lands on the exhaust, create smoke and a fire risk.

causes.name: Valve cover gasket
causes.clues: Oil running down the sides of the engine.

causes.name: Oil pan gasket or drain plug
causes.clues: Drips under the bottom of the engine.

causes.name: Front or rear main seal
causes.clues: Oil at the front of the engine behind the pulley, or where the engine meets the transmission.

you: Put cardboard under the engine overnight to see where it drips.
Track how much oil you add.

result.title: The oil may be dangerously low
result.now: Don't run the engine. Add oil of the type in your owner's manual until it reaches the full mark, a little at a time, rechecking as you go.
if: If it holds a full level, the oil light stays off and the engine sounds normal, that's encouraging but not proof the engine is unharmed. Have the leak or oil use found before relying on the car, and check the level before every start until then.
If it takes a lot of oil, you see oil pouring out, or the engine knocks or ticks loudly, don't run it. Have it towed.
result.why: With little or no oil on the dipstick, the engine's bearings and moving parts aren't being protected. Running it like that can ruin the engine quickly. The smell suggests some of the missing oil is ending up on hot parts.

causes.name: Significant oil leak
causes.clues: Oil spots under the car and oil on the engine.

causes.name: Engine burning oil
causes.clues: Blue-gray exhaust smoke and no visible leak.

causes.name: Missed oil changes
causes.clues: It's been a long time since the last oil change.

you: Add oil and recheck the level.
Look under the car for fresh oil.
shop: Engine noise and oil pressure check

result.title: Get the oil level and leaks checked soon
result.now: Have the oil level checked at a shop or parts store within a few days, and look under the car for fresh oil spots in the meantime.
if: If you see smoke from under the hood or the oil light comes on, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the engine starts knocking or ticking, stop driving it.
result.why: A burning oil smell usually means oil is somewhere it shouldn't be. Knowing the oil level tells you whether it's a small seep or something that could leave the engine short of oil.

causes.name: Oil seeping onto the exhaust
causes.clues: The smell is strongest after a drive, from the hood.

causes.name: Engine burning oil
causes.clues: Blue-gray smoke from the tailpipe.

causes.name: Spill from a recent oil change
causes.clues: Recent service, and the smell is fading.

you: Look for fresh oil spots under the car.
Note when the smell is strongest.
